newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Europe's religious heads say stop poaching flocks.
newsitem.headline: Europe's religious heads say stop poaching flocks.

text.p: Leaders of Europe's main Christian religions appealed to each other on Sunday at the end of a rare inter-denominational conference to stop trying to poach each other's flocks.

"It is necessary...to avoid any competitive endeavour by mutual respect of freedom of conscience," the leaders said in a joint communique at the end of the week-long Second European Ecumenical Conference in the Austrian town of Graz.
The unusually forthright message followed sharp criticism of the Roman Catholic Church's missionary work in eastern Europe from the Russian Orthodox and Armenian churches.

Karekin I, head of the Armenian Church, had accused "some western European Churches" of exploiting the chaos after the break-up of the Soviet Union to boost their own presence rather than cooperate with Orthodox churches which are traditionally strong in the region.
The row prompted the Pope, leader of the world's 960 million Roman Catholics, to send a message to the forum expressing regret at the problems and tensions in eastern Europe.

But shortly before the conference Patriarch Alexiy II of the Russian Orthodox Church called off a meeting with the Pope, saying the churches needed to settle a number of important issues before their heads could meet.
It would have been the first meeting of its kind since the Great Schism split the Christian churches into eastern and western branches in 1054.

The conference, whose theme was reconciliation, attracted well over 10,000 participants, including Alexiy, George Carey, the head of the Anglican church, and top members of the Roman Catholic hierachy.

The Pope said in his message that Christians from east and west could make a "common and yet differentiated" contribution to the spiritual dimension of Europe, and many grass-roots conference participants said the meeting had been of great value.

"It was a terribly important conference coming at a time when colonialisation has ended, communism has changed its face and ecumenism has developed a real face," said a British visitor who had come from London to attend.
The first European ecumenical conference was held in Basle in Switzerland in 1989.
